archetype.name: Bubble Team (possession without finish)
archetype.definition: A team that still wins the puck-possession battle at 5-on-5 but is losing games on percentages and special teams, which leaves it stuck in the middle of a crowded Atlantic, a level below last year's contender.

report.headline: Last year's percentages flipped: Buffalo still drives play but can't score or save.
report.take:
Twelve months ago Buffalo went 50-23-9 with 109 points, finished third on the site and won seven playoff games. Twenty games into Lindy Ruff's next season, the Sabres are 8-8-4, 22nd of 32 and sixth in the Atlantic. The 5-on-5 process does not look like a collapse. Their CF % is 53% (6th in the league) and their xGF % is 50.1%, right at the league mean. Last season those numbers were 49% and 50%, so the possession game has, if anything, improved. They also outshoot opponents slightly, at 27.9 shots for and 26.9 against a game.

The percentages are what changed. Last year Buffalo carried a 102 PDO and its goalies saved 24.5 goals above expected. This year 5-on-5 PDO is 98.1, and all-situations PDO is 97.2, dead last in the league. That comes from both ends: skaters shooting 9.8% (26th) and goalies stopping 87.3% (28th). Special teams add to it. The PP sits at 14.7% against a league average of 22.2%, and the PK at 70.4% is 27th. A team that controls play at even strength while losing badly on both units and in net ends up with a -15 goal differential.

The record actually flatters the differential. Pts vs Goal Diff is +2.5, fourth-highest in the league, so Buffalo has already banked extra points from close games and overtime. Twenty points from twenty games is generous for a team allowing 3.5 a game. The forward group grades D+ and is top-heavy. Tage Thompson has 12 goals, Jack Quinn 9 and Zach Benson 15 points, and after them the scoring falls away quickly. The defense has also allowed more production to opposing centers, relative to expectation, than any team in the league.

The direction since late October is down. November has gone 1-5 at two goals a game, and the last five are 1-3-1. Some of the shooting should come back, given the shot volume and the history. Goaltending is the real swing. Buffalo's GSAx has moved from -31.1 to +25.5 to -9.5 to +24.5 over recent seasons, so last year's elite saving was never a safe baseline. Without a goalie stealing games, this is an 80-something-point team chasing a playoff line that five division rivals are already ahead of.

strengths.title: Still owns the puck at 5-on-5
strengths.body: Buffalo takes 53% of 5-on-5 shot attempts, sixth in the league, and generates more shots than it allows. Its expected-goals share sits right at even rather than leading, which says the volume is not all high-danger. That share is still better than last year's possession numbers, when this team made the playoffs. Possession like this tends to hold, and it gives the scoring something to recover toward.

strengths.title: A blueline that carries minutes
strengths.body: The defense grades A-, the best group on the roster by a distance. Owen Power plays 25.63 minutes a night and ranks 23rd at his position. Rasmus Dahlin runs the power play with 6 PP points in 17 games, and Olen Zellweger posts a 55.7% xGF. The group thins out fast after the top four, but the top four are why the shot share holds up.

strengths.title: A real top line
strengths.body: Thompson has 12 goals on 79 shots and Quinn has 19 points, 7 of them on the power play. Benson's 57.6% xGF is the best among the regular forwards. Benson's 2 goals on 50 shots are the kind of number that corrects itself. This trio is producing; the problem is everyone below it.

concerns.title: Goaltending has gone from asset to hole
concerns.body: The goalies have combined for an .869 save percentage, and the position grades D-. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen has made 11 starts at .867 and -3.3 GSAx. Colten Ellis has been closer to average by GSAx, but his .873 is not a fix. Last year's +24.5 GSAx was a career-type outlier for this franchise rather than its norm, so some recovery is likely but full recovery is not.

concerns.title: Both special-teams units are bottom-six
concerns.body: A 14.7% power play is 29th, and a 70.4% penalty kill is 27th, both several points below league average. The PP was a weak spot in past seasons too, but the PK was 81.9% last year, so the kill is the newer and more fixable problem. Until one of these improves, even-strength edges will keep getting erased.

concerns.title: Close-game luck masking a slide
concerns.body: Buffalo is fourth in points beyond its goal differential, so the .500 points pace is already propped up. Meanwhile November has gone 1-5, with scoring down to two goals a game. If the one-goal results even out before the percentages do, the record could fall faster than the underlying play would suggest.

trend.note: A 7-7 October at just over three goals a game has turned into a 1-5 November. The last five went 1-3-1, scoring dropped to 2.2 a game and the team was shut out in Dallas.

weekAhead.headline: Four straight road games, ending with Florida and Tampa back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The trip starts with the two softest stops. Philadelphia is 28th on the site, scores at the second-lowest rate in the league and loses the shot battle badly. That is the ideal opponent for a shaky goaltending tandem to post a clean night. Washington is a run-and-gun team: ninth in offense but 28th in goals against, with D-grade goaltending. A game there should give Buffalo's slumping shooters chances, and the Capitals have already beaten the Sabres in overtime this year.

The weekend is the problem. Florida and Tampa Bay are both top-six on the site and both limit shots well, and they come on consecutive nights on the road. Tampa beat Buffalo 8-3 eleven days earlier. Splitting the first two and stealing a point on the weekend would be a decent week. Going 2-2 would be a good one.

keyMatchups.title: Philadelphia's punchless attack
keyMatchups.body: The Flyers are 31st in offense, take only 24.6 shots a game and hold a 44.1% xGF. That is the profile Buffalo's possession game should control. If the Sabres can't win this one, the slump is about more than percentages.

keyMatchups.title: Wingers against Washington's leaky net
keyMatchups.body: Washington stops just 88.2% of shots and gives up more production to wingers, relative to expectation, than all but four teams. That sets up well for Quinn and Benson, the wingers who most need goals to show up.

keyMatchups.title: Florida-Tampa back-to-back
keyMatchups.body: Florida kills 85.9% of penalties, fourth in the league, which takes away any power-play lifeline. Tampa runs a 56.3% xGF and beat Buffalo 8-3 on November 11. One small opening: Tampa's PK ranks 25th, a rare spot where Buffalo's weak power play could find goals.

weekAhead.watch: How the starts split between Luukkonen and Ellis across the back-to-back, and whether either can post an above-.900 night against the two best teams on the trip.

restOfSeason.body:
With 62 games left, the current pace of 82 points understates this team in one way and overstates it in another. Last-place all-situations PDO is about as extreme as it gets, and a club that controls 53% of attempts should not keep shooting 9.8%. Expect the goal differential to drift back toward even. The PK should also climb from where it sits, given last year's level. Working the other way, the +2.5 points banked in close games is the kind of edge that rarely repeats. The likely result is a steadier team whose record improves less than its underlying numbers do. I project a finish of roughly 80 to 92 points.

That range lands Buffalo on the outside of the playoff picture unless the goaltending turns. Five Atlantic teams are already clear of them, and Toronto and Detroit are close behind. The ceiling depends on one goalie getting back to average or better, and on scoring from below the top line. The A- blueline and the possession game make a total collapse unlikely. The D+ forward depth and D- goaltending make a return to last year's 109-point level just as unlikely.
swingFactors: Luukkonen or Ellis stabilizing in net
Power play and PK climbing out of the bottom six
Scoring from the forwards below the top line

confidence.note: Only 20 games played. The possession numbers are fairly stable at this sample, but save and shooting percentages are noisy and can swing either way.
